name: the-copy-confirmation-sits-in-the-window-corner
description:
The reported defect: a Link copied card appeared in the SIDEBAR's upper right, not the window's. It was hosted on the sidebar's own document, where .toasts's top and right resolve against that narrow column - no CSS could fix it, because a card in the sidebar's WebContents cannot paint outside it.

The check targets the card's ELEMENT on the window surface rather than a pixel region, and that is deliberate: a pixel probe in the window's corner would pass on anything light-coloured that happened to be there. This reads the card off the /toast document and then compares that widget's own geometry against the window's.

WHY THE WIDGET'S SIZE IS THE MEASUREMENT. The toast widget is sized to the STACK, not to the window - a toast carries a close button so it cannot decline the mouse the way the hint overlay can, and a widget only as large as its cards is not over the page when there are none. So its viewport should be a small card-sized box, not the 1024x680 window. A window-spanning surface would be the earlier defect again, in a new place.

The window's own width is read from the sidebar document, which spans it, so the comparison uses a measured number rather than a constant that drifts.

actions.note: copies the active tab's link, which is what raises the confirmation

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); return t ? t.textContent : 'no card'; })()
actions.note: The element itself, on the window-level surface.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } const r = c.getBoundingClientRect(); return String(r.left >= -1 && r.top >= -1 && r.right <= window.innerWidth + 1 && r.bottom <= window.innerHeight + 1); })()
actions.note: Placed immediately after the card is seen, NOT at the end of the run: a confirmation dismisses itself after CONFIRM_MS, 1400ms, and an earlier version of this scenario asked several evals later and got 'no card'. Every reading of a transient card has to happen inside its own lifetime.
the widget's own box. Sized to the stack, so this should be card-sized rather than window-sized.

actions.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (!c) { return 'no card'; } const r = c.getBoundingClientRect(); return Math.round(r.left) + ',' + Math.round(r.top) + ' ' + Math.round(r.width) + 'x' + Math.round(r.height); })()
actions.note: Diagnostic that became an assertion. It read -24,44 166x48 inside a 171x48 widget - the stack still applied its window-corner insets of top 44 and right 14 inside its own surface, so most of the card was clipped outside it. The card was on the right surface and unreadable.
the sidebar's own width, which is the column the card used to be trapped in

a stack-sized widget, not a window-spanning one. 700 is well above any card and well below the 1024 window, so this fails loudly if the surface ever grows to span the window - which would be a dead band in a new place.

assertions.desc: The confirmation card exists on the window-level toast surface, read as an element rather than as pixels
the widget is sized to its stack. A window-spanning toast surface would swallow page clicks everywhere it covers, since a toast has a close button and cannot decline the mouse.

the card fits within its own surface. The widget is sized to the stack, so any inset the stack keeps for a window corner pushes the card out of the very widget that is meant to show it - which is how it first read, at -24,44 in a 171x48 box.

assertions.label: the-confirmation-was-raised
assertions.note: the one line every confirmation shares, so the reading above is tied to a real raise
